15 A power station using coal as fuel has an average power output of 3000 MW. Coal is supplied by
20 trains each day. The efficiency of the station in converting the thermal energy released from
the coal to electrical energy is 26%.
A mass of 1.0 kg of coal will release 33 MJ of thermal energy when burnt.
Which mass of coal does each train bring?
A
2.5 × 104
kg
B
6.3 × 104
kg
C
1.5 × 106
kg
D
3.0 × 107
kg

9702/12/O/N/19

hints: Notice that $3000 \text{ MW}$ is the useful electrical power output sustained for one day, so convert one day to $86400 \text{ s}$ and use $E = Pt$ for daily electrical energy.
Use the 26% efficiency as $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{thermal input}$, so the required thermal energy from coal is larger than the electrical energy by a factor of $1/0.26$.
Convert the daily thermal energy to daily mass with $33 \text{ MJ}$ per $1.0 \text{ kg}$, then divide that total by 20 trains to get mass per train.
walkthrough: Find the useful electrical energy delivered in one day. $P = 3000 \text{ MW} = 3.0 \times 10^{9} \text{ W}$ and $t = 24 \times 3600 = 86400 \text{ s}$, so $E_{electrical} = Pt = 3.0 \times 10^{9} \times 86400 \approx 2.59 \times 10^{14} \text{ J}$.

Find the thermal energy that must be released by the coal. With $\text{efficiency} = 0.26 = E_{electrical}/E_{thermal}$, then $E_{thermal} = E_{electrical}/0.26 \approx 2.59 \times 10^{14}/0.26 \approx 9.97 \times 10^{14} \text{ J}$.

Find the total mass burnt per day. Since $1.0 \text{ kg}$ gives $33 \text{ MJ} = 33 \times 10^{6} \text{ J}$, then $m_{total} = 9.97 \times 10^{14} / (33 \times 10^{6}) \approx 3.0 \times 10^{7} \text{ kg}$.
Find the mass per train. With 20 trains per day, $m_{train} = 3.0 \times 10^{7}/20 \approx 1.5 \times 10^{6} \text{ kg}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Far too small to sustain $3000 \text{ MW}$ for a day; it results from mishandling power, time and the $33 \text{ MJ kg}^{-1}$ energy content.

B.explanation: Far too small for 20 trains per day; it is close to forgetting to multiply by $86400 \text{ s}$ or to divide correctly by the 26% efficiency.

C.explanation: Gives about $3.0 \times 10^{7} \text{ kg}$ per day divided by 20, matching the thermal input required for the daily electrical output at 26% efficiency.

D.explanation: This is the total mass of coal burnt in one whole day; it still needs to be divided by 20 to give the mass brought by each train.
